decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Arthur points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Arthur keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Arthur a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Price check on your dignity
decisions.situation: In a quiet shop, you loudly announce that Arthur has a bottom. Several shoppers appear to know already.

choices.label: Repeat it for anyone who missed it
Try an extremely loud whisper
Give Arthur a hug

result.title: Full coverage
result.body: Arthur finishes shopping at record speed.

journal.text: I made a loud announcement about Arthur in a shop.

decisions.title: The volcano has escaped
decisions.situation: Your classroom volcano erupts across Alice’s desk. Helena grabs a towel. You have made geology personal.

choices.label: Help clean the desk
Measure how far it went
Add the rest of the mixture

result.title: Containment team
result.body: You clean together. Helena asks you to use less mixture next time.

journal.text: I cleaned up after our classroom volcano flooded Alice’s desk.

decisions.title: Glitter lockdown
decisions.situation: You spill a pot of glitter during a class project. Helena finds some inside a closed book.

choices.label: Help clean every desk
Make a paper funnel for next time
Try blowing it away

result.title: Still sparkling
result.body: You clean until the bell. There is probably some glitter left in the building forever.

journal.text: I helped clean a classroom after spilling glitter everywhere.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Arthur’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Tell Arthur what happened
Offer to help repair it
Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Arthur is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Arthur’s mug.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Arthur plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of
Trade one song each
Give a brutally concise review

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Arthur.

journal.text: I listened to Arthur’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Arthur finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Watch it together
Ask to keep the recording private
Defend the bath theory

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Arthur remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Arthur.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

choices.label: Ask whether anyone actually knows
Mute it and step away
Forward it for a reaction

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: Selective honesty
decisions.situation: Arthur has marked a correct answer wrong and a wrong answer right. The mistakes cancel out. You could mention both, or suddenly become very interested in only one.

choices.label: Point out both mistakes
Get the answers explained properly
Ask for the lost marks. Hide the free ones.

result.title: No profit, better reputation
result.body: Arthur corrects both marks and thanks you for being honest. Your grade stays exactly where it was.

journal.text: I showed Arthur two marking mistakes that cancelled each other out.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Brasília, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Brasília.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Brasília offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Practice grief
decisions.situation: At a free estate-planning demonstration, volunteers act as fictional heirs. Your card says “loving relative”. The person beside you is already asking what the imaginary house is worth.

choices.label: Play the grieving relative sincerely
Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Congratulations, almost
decisions.situation: A caller says you have won a fortune in a lottery you never entered. To release the prize, they need a “small verification payment”. They sound personally hurt that you have questions.

choices.label: End the call before sharing anything
Ask how they feel about their life choices
Dictate a completely invented forty-letter name

result.title: Your fortune remains imaginary
result.body: You hang up. The only thing you lose is the chance to hear which payment methods the imaginary lottery prefers.

journal.text: I ended a suspicious lottery call without sending money.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Brasília needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Brasília.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Brasília takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

result.title: Medical care arranged
